question.prompt: How many integer solutions of the inequality \(x^2-4>0\) have an absolute value less than 4?

solutions.explanation: \(x^2>4\) gives \(x<-2\) or \(x>2\). With the additional restriction \(-4<x<4\), the only integer solutions are \(-3\) and 3, giving 2 in total.
solutions.title: Solve the inequality and apply the restriction

solutions.explanation: The condition \(|x|<4\) restricts the integer candidates to \(-3,-2,-1,0,1,2,3\). Substituting them into \(x^2-4\) gives \(5,0,-3,-4,-3,0,5\), respectively. Only the values at \(x=-3\) and \(x=3\) are positive, so there are \(2\) solutions.
solutions.title: Check the seven possible integers
